edits.find: - **Still open, and not part of any slice above.**
edits.replace: - **Closed since 21 August, and this file was the stale half of it.**

edits.find: tracks transactional `replaceTrack` ordering after a failed recompile.
edits.replace: was completed by [#178](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/pull/178), which landed the staged replacement, and this file went on calling it open for two weeks: a debt list carrying another issue's state is re-read against that issue rather than against itself, which is the rule the guide-debt list in this file already earned once. C3's widening of it is real and closed by ADR-066, and it is not the rollback path: both shapes of a failed recompile are correct, and what the declined build stopped doing was dropping a live value write.

edits.find: Whether load should seed a flush too is unasked and unanswered; it has no members yet when it would.
edits.replace: Whether load should seed a flush too is decided rather than unasked: it does not, and that is a refusal rather than an omission, because there is no member to publish to at load and an empty seed set is not a cheap flush. The member arrives at `mount`, which is where the seed went, so a loaded node publishes at rest once it is mounted and the asymmetry was never about load at all. It was that a node mounted by a commit is seeded by `#apply` while a node mounted by a caller was seeded by nobody. The seed is at the public verb and never at `#mountNode`, because a commit already seeds the node it mounted. See ADR-066.

edits.find: Every structural edit drops it too, for the same reason: they route through `#replaceTrack`, which retains a fresh entry with no overlay.
edits.replace: Every structural edit drops it too, and the timeline build is what does the dropping rather than the retained entry: a fresh Track carries no mask and no patched timeline, and `#replaceTrack` retains an entry recording neither. So the recompile predicate builds when a live write is in force even though the compiled input did not move, because the step it skips owned two things. Without that, the four binding verbs kept an override the paragraph above says they drop, and a cleared overlay over a still-patched timeline is a freeze no public verb can revert. See ADR-066.

edits.find: - A debt list is a measurement, not a ledger.
edits.replace: - A debt list is a measurement, not a ledger, and that reaches the state of anything it cites. This file called [issue #176](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/176) open and tracked for two weeks after it was completed, and part 6 of the re-review repeated it, so a plan was written around a fix that was owed to nobody. An entry naming another issue is re-read against that issue before it is cited.

edits.find: - Every earlier slice's red and green run ids live in the pull request that landed it.
edits.replace:
- A node publishing at rest at the mount: `RA-100` through `RA-102` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/mount-flush-seed.test.ts`. `RA-102` is green on purpose as the equivalence half, holding a structural add at exactly one flush, which is what fails if the seed is put at the attach rather than at the public verb. `RA-101` is an oracle rather than a counter, because a sequence that moved proves a flush happened and only a patch proves the flush was about that node.
- The live write a declined build used to drop: `RA-103` through `RA-105` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/declined-build-write-drop.test.ts`. `RA-104` is green on purpose as the equivalence half, holding a binding edit on a node with no live write at zero builds, so the fix cannot be "always build". `RA-105` is the ordering guard and is green on both sides, because the resolve runs today and must keep running; it fails only against the short-circuit that would skip it.
- Every earlier slice's red and green run ids live in the pull request that landed it.
